verdict.rationale: Glama documents a hosted, no-login browser MCP Inspector. It connects to remote Streamable HTTP and SSE endpoints, supports tools and other MCP features with OAuth, bearer, or custom-header auth, executes tools interactively with a JSON-RPC protocol log, and can reach local servers through an mcp-proxy tunnel. That covers exercising a server's tools before integrating it. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the inspector's tool execution (all evidence is vendor documentation).

support.subject: As a developer, I can exercise an MCP server's tools from a browser-based inspector or playground before integrating it

citations.quote: Test any MCP server from your browser. Supports every Model Context Protocol feature, including tools, resources, prompts, tasks, elicitation, sampling, and OAuth 2.1.
Glama's hosted inspector connects to remote Streamable HTTP and SSE endpoints so you can inspect available capabilities and test requests interactively
Inspect any MCP server directly from your browser. No login required.
Test your local MCP servers with the inspector by exposing them via a public tunnel using mcp-proxy.
